properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Cottle County in northwestern Texas...
Southeastern Motley County in northwestern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM CDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable. Expect
many areas of slow moving or standing water. It will take several
hours for all the water from these storms to work through local
drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1156 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
significant rainfall accumulations from heavy rain due to
thunderstorms that occurred over the past 24 hours. Flooding is
already occurring in the warned area. Up to 5 inches of rain have
fallen. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms are
expected to continue through early Thursday morning, which may
bring up to 2 inches of additional rainfall to the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Paducah, Swearingen, Chalk, Delwin and Hackberry.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY NEW FIRE STARTS
THURSDAY THROUGH SATURDAY DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY STRONG SANTA
ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.Moderate to locally strong Santa Ana winds will quickly develop
on Thursday, peak Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon,
then slowly weaken through the weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will
settle over the region and dry out any effects of the recent
rains. Red Flag Warnings are in effect for most of Los Angeles
and Ventura Counties Thursday through Saturday, and for interior
Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo Counties for Friday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Western Santa Monica Mountains Recreational
Area, Eastern Santa Monica Mountains Recreational Area, Santa
Susana Mountains, Southern Ventura County Mountains, Northern
Ventura County Mountains, Interstate 5 Corridor, Western San
Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor, Eastern San Gabriel
Mountains, Western Antelope Valley Foothills and Eastern
Antelope Valley Foothills.

* TIMING...From 6 AM Thursday to 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast to east 20 to 40 mph with gusts of 50 to 70
mph, strongest Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

properties.headline: Typhoon Watch issued October 15 at 2:42PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...A TYPHOON WATCH IS NOW IN EFFECT FOR THE MARIANAS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
A Typhoon Watch has now been issued for Guam, Rota, Tinian and
Saipan in the Mariana Islands.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and
recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon watch is in effect for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan in
the Mariana Islands.

A Typhoon Watch means that Typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or greater, are possible within the next 48 hours somewhere
within the specified areas.

All persons in the watch areas should review their preparedness
plan and begin to take actions to prepare for conditions as
indicated by your local forecast and additional details.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 1 PM ChST...the center of Tropical Depression 29W was located
near latitude 10.8N...longitude 158.9E. This was about 970 miles
east of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 285 degrees, at
13 mph. 29W is expected to make a turn toward the west over the next
couple of days. Storm intensity was 35 mph. 29W is expected to begin
to intensify Friday.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
A Typhoon Watch has now been issued. A more detailed statement will
follow shortly.
properties.instruction:
.

For those under a watch, now is the time to initiate preparations
according to your typhoon disaster plan specific to your home or
business.

For those nearby, review your typhoon disaster plan and become ready
to act if a watch or a warning is later issued for your area.

It is important to actively listen for forthcoming information
from your local National Weather Service office and emergency
management agency.

properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Glasscock County in western Texas...
Southeastern Howard County in western Texas...
Mitchell County in western Texas...
Scurry County in western Texas...

* Until 230 AM CDT.

* At 1125 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Big Spring, Snyder, Colorado City, Coahoma, Loraine, Forsan, Lake
Colorado City, Lake Colorado City State Park, Colorado City
Airport, Champion Creek Reservoir, Sand Springs, Inadale,
Westbrook, Cuthbert, Buford, Ira, Dunn, Knapp and Winston Field.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
